narratives.Overview:
1. Widen command. `scope:record-approved-scope -- --add-path

` (repeatable) is the widen. Run by an operator in the story's bound worktree, it creates a temporary detached checkout of the delivery tip outside the repository's worktree list for lifecycle purposes. There it writes each new path, and the story's own record paths `.deft/approved-scope/.json` and `.deft/approved-scope/.intent.json`, into the brief's `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` (no duplicates, existing entries kept), then mints the approval record and intent preimage for that brief as the verb does today. It commits only the brief, the record and the preimage, pushes a new `widen/` branch, opens a brief-only PR whose body names the story and the added paths, prints the PR URL, and removes the checkout. It never writes an occupancy lease, a worker assignment or a story binding, and the bound worktree is not changed. After that PR merges, the story rebases and the merge-base brief carries the paths. The human-presence gate, record shape and intent preimage are unchanged; without `--add-path` the verb behaves as today. 2. Why that PR passes. At one-PR proof level `mint`, `evaluateMintLevelRecord` admits the same-PR record for the widened brief, and membership then uses its `file_scope`, which lists the two record files, as the documented one-PR rule already requires (`content/docs/scope-provenance.md` 98). The change set holds no story product, so the class-4 protected-path mix does not arise. The record paths are not production-class, so the production check does not count them. No check is changed. 3. Confession in the bound worktree. `scope:confess` from #6644 (bound lean 6969795502 item 6) runs in the story's bound worktree as an agent verb with that arc's refusals unchanged, and writes no approval record. The intent compare (`compareScalars` on the extracted `plan.acceptance`) leaves `acceptance.confessions` out on both sides; every other field of `plan.acceptance`, `commands` included, stays pinned. 4. Confession rides the product PR. The brief diff that item 3 writes in the bound worktree is committed with the product change. The Write/Edit fence on `xbrief/active/` is unchanged, and item 3 does not change `file_scope`. 5. Arced criteria after acceptance. Ingest, its harvest, the Target-digest check and the live identity check are unchanged. An operator drop of an accepted Bound or Acceptance Criteria item is recorded after ingest with the #6644 `acceptance-disposition` grant as `not_applicable` and a reason on that item's clause. An addition or rewording needs a later lean. The issue body is not edited to record either. 6. Stale-target refusal text. When ingest refuses with `stale-target`, the message adds three remedies: restore the issue body to the arced text; record an operator drop after ingest with the `acceptance-disposition` grant (`--disposition not_applicable`); or post a later lean for an addition or rewording. The check itself is unchanged. ## Acceptance Criteria - Given `scope:record-approved-scope -- --add-path p` run by an operator in a bound worktree, then a brief-only PR is opened whose brief lists `p`, `.deft/approved-scope/.json` and `.deft/approved-scope/.intent.json` in `file_scope` once each, and whose approval record names that brief. - Given that run, then the PR changes only the brief, its approval record and its intent preimage; the bound worktree has no new changes; no occupancy lease, assignment or binding is written; and the temporary checkout is removed. - Given that PR on a merge base with `onePrScopeProof: mint`, then `verify:scope-provenance` and `verify:class-checks` both admit its change set. - Given `scope:record-approved-scope` without `--add-path`, then its output is the same as before this change. - Given an agent or CI shell running `scope:record-approved-scope --add-path`, then the gate refuses, no checkout, branch or PR is made, and the brief is not changed. - Given `scope:confess` run in a story's bound worktree, then it writes the confession as #6644 specifies and writes no approval record. - Given a story with an intent pin on the merge base and a product change set whose only brief change is a new `acceptance.confessions` entry, then `verify:scope-provenance` reports no `intent-drift`; a change to `plan.acceptance.commands` in the same position still reports it. - Given an arced issue whose body was edited after the accepted record, when `issue:ingest` refuses with `stale-target`, then the message names the three remedies. - Given an ingested arced story and an `acceptance-disposition` grant with `--disposition not_applicable` on the clause of an accepted item the operator dropped, then `scope:complete` treats that clause as #6644 specifies and the harvest, pin and identity check are unchanged.

- Narrowing class checks or membership to free the record pair (comments 6984164781 finding 1 and 6984561550 finding 1, smallest changes; the operator chose the file-list rule and the brief-only widen).
- An agent-runnable acceptance-command writer; human merge review as its only control (comment 6970307319 finding 2).
- Any acceptance-command writer or acceptance-command pin change in this story; that question is #6666 (operator resume 6983878826; comments 6970477768 finding 1 and 6970667387 findings 1 and 2).
- A comment-based drop of accepted items before ingest; a harvest that subtracts items named in a comment; positional drops that renumber slice references (comment 6970307319 finding 3).
- A refresh of a brief from the issue body; re-pinning the Target-digest to an edited body.
- Opening the Write/Edit fence on `xbrief/active/` to the story's own agent.
- Confession edits in the product PR that leave a pinned `plan.acceptance` to fail the intent check (comment 6970477768 finding 1).
- Making `scope:confess` mint a human approval record.

Target-digest: sha256:d6ee5bdf397a7c7c243af1b00149594f1bf7f07e96b4a2f5b8004008c6099159 dispatch-sha: c569ca24830474d1998bb7d19e588aad7ee063fc dest: .deft-scratch/worktrees/arc-6643 (pinKind origin-default, process-only-no-install) arc-mode: no-ingest yolo-standing: on charter: open critique spend-recommend: N=1 spend: N=1 spend-ask: resolved spend-why: three narrow pains on the brief-write and ingest paths; one critic of a different model family (Grok), as the overnight envelope sets. materiality-bar: open target-kind: issue ceiling-kind: comment-id verification-path: pin-read git show c569ca24830474d1998bb7d19e588aad7ee063fc: + dest cwd-without-occupy pain: P1, P2, P3 ## In plain English Three routine changes to a story cost an extra pull request each. To widen a story's file list, stamp an acceptance command, or confess sentences that are not criteria, a worker today opens a second, brief-only PR from a worktree that is not bound to the story, because the bound worktree cannot write its own brief. Separately, once a design arc on an issue is accepted, the operator has no sanctioned way to drop an item from the accepted design before ingest: editing the issue body makes ingest refuse with a stale-target digest error. The recommended fix makes the local write fence admit a widened brief on the same same-PR human mint that CI already admits, lets the existing brief-writing verbs run in the bound worktree so their change rides the product PR, and lets the operator record a drop-only amendment as a comment that ingest applies, with the issue body left as arced. The issue has no `## Acceptance Criteria` heading. The three pains below are derived from its `## Expected` section: P1 and P2 split its first bullet (widen; acceptance command and confession), P3 is its second bullet. ## Pains - P1 — A story-bound worktree cannot widen its own brief's `file_scope` in the product PR; the widen needs a separate brief-only PR from an unbound worktree (#6611, the #6221 widen worktree). - P2 — A story-bound worktree cannot stamp an acceptance command on its own brief or confess its unmapped sentences in the product PR; each needs a separate brief-only PR from an unbound worktree (#6624, #6639). - P3 — After an arc's synthesis is accepted, the operator has no sanctioned way to correct the arced criteria before ingest: a body edit gives a stale-target refusal at ingest (#6602, operator decision comment 6967286497). ## Constraints (not pains) - No new gate, grant template, refusal or policy flag. Narrowing an existing check, or making two checks agree, is allowed. - An agent must not be able to widen its own fence or remove a reviewed criterion without an operator act. - Do not contradict the accepted sibling arc on #6644 (synthesis 6969950740, bound lean 6969795502): the `acceptance-disposition` grant gains `not_applicable` and `waived`, and a new `scope:confess` verb writes `acceptance.confessions`; a refresh of a brief from the issue body was rejected there, because an issue edit is not an operator mint. That arc's fixes after ingest are not redesigned here. - #6609 (ingest harvest), #6645 (story marks) and #6642 (merge path) are separate; this arc must not depend on them. ## Anchors at the dispatch SHA - `packages/core/src/policy/one-pr-scope-proof.ts` 1-20: the `mint` level is for "landing a new or widened brief with its code in one PR"; the local write fence admits only a brief absent from the merge base (#6361). This repo's PROJECT-DEFINITION sets `onePrScopeProof: "mint"`. - `packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts` 758-838 `loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase`: a brief on the merge base gets its merge-base `file_scope` and the head copy is ignored; 699-756 `loadOnePrMintFence` (same-PR mint) runs only on the `missing` branch (813-820). - `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` 1-48 (header: head brief edits do not widen; one-PR mint level), 1289-1335: a same-PR mint at the `mint` level is admitted for any modified active brief with a rewritten approval record, without a base-absence condition; 1888-1893: the production fence then uses that mint scope. - `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/base-fence.ts` 263: "head brief edits do not widen the fence (#4956 / #6221)". - `packages/core/src/scope/lifecycle-write.ts` 56-76: "xbrief/active/ on a product PR is correct". - `packages/core/src/scope/bind-clause.ts` (`scope:bind-clause`): an existing verb that writes an active brief. No `deft` verb writes `plan.acceptance.commands` (verb names searched under `packages/` at the pin). - `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts` 2711-2790: for a completed arc, ingest harvests the cited Spec-path lean (Bound remedy, then Acceptance Criteria), and separately checks the lean's `Target-digest` against the live issue body; 1784-1790: the acceptance text is taken from that harvest, not the body. `packages/core/src/design-critique/completed-arc-record.ts` 784-850 `evaluateTargetDigestAdmission`. - `content/contracts/design-critique.md` 289-324 (closed role set `triage|critic|parent`), 603-649 (bind and ingest clearance cite the latest successor lean). ## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique) - F1. Fence parity for a widen (P1). `loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase` runs the same same-PR mint check for a brief that is on the merge base: when the merge-base level is `mint` and the head mint record for the brief's plan id matches the head brief exactly (`evaluateMintLevelRecord`, the evaluator CI uses), the fence uses the mint's `file_scope`; otherwise the merge-base `file_scope` as today. CI is unchanged. Level `off` keeps today's two-PR widen. - F2. One operator step for a widen (P1). The operator runs the existing human-presence mint verb (`packages/runtime/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts`, `human-presence-mint.ts`) in the bound worktree with the new paths (`scope:record-approved-scope -- --add-path

`, repeatable). It writes the paths into the head brief's `file_scope` and mints the record for that head brief in one step. Agents cannot run it, as today. The brief, mint record and product change land in one PR. - F3. Brief verbs in the bound worktree (P2). `scope:confess` (from #6644) and a new `scope:set-acceptance-command -- --command ""` (repeatable; writes `plan.acceptance.commands` and `none_stated: false`, prints the old and new list) run in the story's bound worktree and write the story's own active brief, like `scope:bind-clause`. Their diff rides the product PR. The Write/Edit fence on the brief path is unchanged. The human merge review sees the brief diff. - F4. Drop-only operator amendment (P3). After the accepted record, a `role: parent` comment whose operative line is `design-critique: operator amendment, because ` and that lists `drops: Bound item N` or `drops: Acceptance Criteria item N` lines may cite the bound lean. Does that reopen the #4956 / #6221 rule that head brief edits do not widen, given CI already admits the same mint at 1289-1335, and is `requireHumanMerge: false` on this repo a hole? 2. F3 lets an agent set its own acceptance command. Can an agent self-grade a story that way (a trivially green command), and is the human merge review enough, or should only the operator run that verb? 3. Does F4 contradict the #6644 rejection of a refresh from the issue body? Does a `role: parent` amendment after the accepted record trip `later-arc-in-flight`, the citation grammar, or the path-1 gate, and is drop-only the right limit?

## In plain English

A worktree bound to a story cannot change that story's brief, so widening the file list, stamping an acceptance command, or confessing a sentence that is not a criterion each takes a second, brief-only pull request. After a design arc is accepted, editing the issue body makes ingest refuse on a stale digest, so a reviewed item also has no sanctioned drop before the brief is created.

The recommended mechanism does not hold.

The widen is not safe as fence parity, and it does not relieve that pain. Membership already accepts a same-PR mint of the head brief. The production check still requires every minted path to sit inside the brief already on the merge base, and it skips that check only when the merge-base file list is empty, which is the new-brief case. Teaching the local fence to follow the head mint for a brief already on the base lets the worktree write files the pull-request check still refuses. Leaving that check unchanged leaves the extra pull request for any path past the existing extra-file allowance. This repository does not require a human merge. The policy text already says that, in that case, CI verifies nothing human. Following the head mint on the production check would remove the remaining backstop. The proposed add-path flag is not on the mint verb. An operator mint records the brief as it already stands.

An agent can self-grade with the proposed command verb. A shell command that is not a classified file write is allowed, and the process then writes the brief, which is how bind-clause already works. A command outside the small no-op list that exits 0 becomes an executable pass and clears a story whose clauses were never verified. Human merge review is not a control this repository runs. The confession verb from the accepted sibling arc can still run in the bound worktree under that arc's refuse rules. The command writer needs the existing human-presence gate.

The drop comment does not revive the rejected refresh-from-the-issue-body verb. In the shape described, a parent comment does not by itself look like a later arc, a new lean, or a path-1 retarget, and a closed-form citation on that comment does not reselect the lean. It does contradict the reason the sibling arc refused a body edit. The completed-arc check does not read author identity, so anyone who can comment can drop a reviewed item, and a comment is a weaker act than an issue edit. Ingest would pin the shortened list while the live compare re-reads the whole accepted lean and refuses the brief for the whole pre-merge window. Drop-only is the right limit on content: adding or rewording still needs a later lean. The authority and the live compare are missing. The sibling arc already records an operator drop after ingest with the acceptance-disposition grant, and that path leaves the harvest and the pin unchanged.

### 1. Same-PR mint parity on a brief already on the merge base (blocks-the-design)

Evidence. `loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase` (`packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts` 770–837) gives a brief that exists on the merge base that commit's file list and ignores the working-tree copy. `loadOnePrMintFence` (710–756) runs only on the missing branch (813–819). When that mint admits, the fence sets `onePrMint.admitted` and `resolveAuthority` (`packages/core/src/policy/write-fence-budget.ts` 145–146) uses the mint file list with no second list. A merge-base mint, by contrast, keeps the brief as that second list (183–188). CI's anti-forgery carve-out admits the same mint for any modified active brief with a rewritten approval record and no base-absence test (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` 1289–1335), and membership then uses that mint list alone (1541–1544; `evaluateApprovedScopeMembership` in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/base-fence.ts` 498–513 passes no `alsoAllowlist`). The production fence still receives that mint and intersects it with the merge-base brief (`evaluate.ts` 44 and 1888–1902; `base-fence.ts` 194–200). The intersection is skipped only when the merge-base file list is empty (`base-fence.ts` 190–192). The over-budget detail still says head brief edits do not widen the fence (263). `alsoAllowlist` is the second list a path must match (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/extra-path-admission.ts` 79–84, 134–142). This repository's project definition sets `requireHumanMerge` false and `onePrScopeProof` to `mint` (`xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` 23894–23895). The mint-level control line for that policy says CI verifies nothing human (`packages/core/src/policy/one-pr-scope-proof.ts` 11–20 and 62–75). The header's "new or widened brief" (4–8) is implemented as the absent-brief mint. `scope:record-approved-scope` usage has no add-path flag; it writes the approval record for the brief as it stands (`packages/runtime/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts` 67–74). Human presence refuses an agent or CI shell (`packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts` 280–312).

Failure mode. Two implementations both fail. If the on-base fence copies the absent-brief admit, the worktree can write every path in the head mint while the production check still intersects the merge-base brief, so the agent writes files the pull request refuses as over budget. The same documented shell-form residual that already reaches local admission for a new brief (policy lines 18–20 and 71–75) would then reach every bound story. If the fence stores the widened list but leaves `onePrMint` unset, a story with no merge-base mint record becomes a concrete allowlist of that widened list (`write-fence-budget.ts` 161–162), which is the same local widen, and a story that already has a merge-base mint stays intersected, so the new paths remain extras. The production check does not gain the empty-base skip, because an on-base brief has a non-empty file list. Making the production check follow the head mint, which is the reading of "make the two checks agree," deletes the intersection the code comments name as the rule that a broader mint does not widen (`base-fence.ts` 194–197). With human merge not required, that check is the CI backstop the policy text still names. The operator mint cannot close the gap: it does not edit the file list, and a record that matched a widened head brief would still be the mint CI cannot tell from a file an agent wrote.

Disposition. The fence-parity limb and the one-step mint cannot bind as the widen remedy. Binding them either leaves the extra brief pull request for paths past the existing allowance, or lets the bound worktree write paths the pull-request check still refuses. Teaching that check to follow the head mint reopens the on-base widen rule while this repository's merge-base policy has CI verify nothing human.

The strongest case for parity is that membership already admits this mint, and agreeing two checks is inside the stated constraints. That case describes membership. The production check is the check that still intersects. What would flip this reading is a merge-base policy on which the human merge is already the named control (`one-pr-scope-proof.ts` 62–64) together with the production check following the same mint. This repository's recorded policy is the other control line. No deterministic control that CI can fail closed on, short of a new gate, showed up in these readers. The road left in place is the one the code already has: an on-base widen is a brief that lands on the merge base before the new product files, and same-PR paths inside the extra-file allowance stay on that allowance.

### 2. An agent-set acceptance command clears an unverified story (blocks-the-design)

Evidence. `classifyShellWriteTargets` (`packages/core/src/hooks/shell-write-targets.ts` 225–243) classifies Set-Content, Add-Content, Out-File, a Python path write, and WriteAllText. The shell gate walks only those destinations (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 3537). `scope:bind-clause` writes the brief from inside the process with `atomicWriteBrief` (`packages/core/src/scope/bind-clause.ts` 297) after setting `artifact_path` on a clause already in scope. The proposed command verb is specified to run the same way and to write `plan.acceptance.commands` with `none_stated` false. ## Summary

A story-bound worktree cannot edit its own brief, and an arced issue's acceptance criteria have no sanctioned correction path. Both force extra PRs and stops for routine changes.

## Evidence

- Widens, acceptance-command stamps and confessions on a story each needed a separate brief-only PR from an unbound worktree: #6611 (activation), #6624 (acceptance command), #6639 (confession of unmapped sentences on #6601). A widen worktree for #6221 that was bound by mistake held a lease and had to be abandoned.
- Editing an arced issue's body gives a stale-target digest refusal at ingest, because ingest is digest-bound to the arced body. So there is no way to correct the criteria of an arced issue (#6601 and #6602 are examples; #6609 is the related harvest bug).

## Expected

- A story-bound worktree may amend its own brief (widen, acceptance command, confession) in the same PR as the product change, or a single documented verb does it without an unbound worktree.
- An arced issue's criteria can be corrected by a sanctioned verb (for example re-ingest against a recorded operator comment) instead of a stale-target refusal. Prefer removing a step over adding a gate.

## Workaround used today

Brief-only PRs from unbound worktrees (#6611, #6624, #6639); operator changes recorded as issue comments instead of body edits.

Refs #6601, #6602, #6609, #6611, #6624, #6639

sentences:
Widen command. `scope:record-approved-scope -- --add-path

` (repeatable) is the widen. Run by an operator in the story's bound worktree, it creates a temporary detached checkout of the delivery tip outside the repository's worktree list for lifecycle purposes. There it writes each new path, and the story's own record paths `.deft/approved-scope/.json` and `.deft/approved-scope/.intent.json`, into the brief's `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` (no duplicates, existing entries kept), then mints the approval record and intent preimage for that brief as the verb does today. It commits only the brief, the record and the preimage, pushes a new `widen/` branch, opens a brief-only PR whose body names the story and the added paths, prints the PR URL, and removes the checkout. It never writes an occupancy lease, a worker assignment or a story binding, and the bound worktree is not changed. After that PR merges, the story rebases and the merge-base brief carries the paths. The human-presence gate, record shape and intent preimage are unchanged; without `--add-path` the verb behaves as today.

Why that PR passes. At one-PR proof level `mint`, `evaluateMintLevelRecord` admits the same-PR record for the widened brief, and membership then uses its `file_scope`, which lists the two record files, as the documented one-PR rule already requires (`content/docs/scope-provenance.md` 98). The change set holds no story product, so the class-4 protected-path mix does not arise. The record paths are not production-class, so the production check does not count them. No check is changed.

Confession in the bound worktree. `scope:confess` from #6644 (bound lean 6969795502 item 6) runs in the story's bound worktree as an agent verb with that arc's refusals unchanged, and writes no approval record. The intent compare (`compareScalars` on the extracted `plan.acceptance`) leaves `acceptance.confessions` out on both sides; every other field of `plan.acceptance`, `commands` included, stays pinned.

Confession rides the product PR. The brief diff that item 3 writes in the bound worktree is committed with the product change. The Write/Edit fence on `xbrief/active/` is unchanged, and item 3 does not change `file_scope`.

Arced criteria after acceptance. Ingest, its harvest, the Target-digest check and the live identity check are unchanged. An operator drop of an accepted Bound or Acceptance Criteria item is recorded after ingest with the #6644 `acceptance-disposition` grant as `not_applicable` and a reason on that item's clause. An addition or rewording needs a later lean. The issue body is not edited to record either.

Stale-target refusal text. When ingest refuses with `stale-target`, the message adds three remedies: restore the issue body to the arced text; record an operator drop after ingest with the `acceptance-disposition` grant (`--disposition not_applicable`); or post a later lean for an addition or rewording. The check itself is unchanged.

Given `scope:record-approved-scope -- <brief> --add-path p` run by an operator in a bound worktree, then a brief-only PR is opened whose brief lists `p`, `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` and `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.intent.json` in `file_scope` once each, and whose approval record names that brief.

Given that run, then the PR changes only the brief, its approval record and its intent preimage; the bound worktree has no new changes; no occupancy lease, assignment or binding is written; and the temporary checkout is removed.
Given that PR on a merge base with `onePrScopeProof: mint`, then `verify:scope-provenance` and `verify:class-checks` both admit its change set.
Given `scope:record-approved-scope` without `--add-path`, then its output is the same as before this change.
Given an agent or CI shell running `scope:record-approved-scope --add-path`, then the gate refuses, no checkout, branch or PR is made, and the brief is not changed.
Given `scope:confess` run in a story's bound worktree, then it writes the confession as #6644 specifies and writes no approval record.

Given a story with an intent pin on the merge base and a product change set whose only brief change is a new `acceptance.confessions` entry, then `verify:scope-provenance` reports no `intent-drift`; a change to `plan.acceptance.commands` in the same position still reports it.
Given an arced issue whose body was edited after the accepted record, when `issue:ingest` refuses with `stale-target`, then the message names the three remedies.

Given an ingested arced story and an `acceptance-disposition` grant with `--disposition not_applicable` on the clause of an accepted item the operator dropped, then `scope:complete` treats that clause as #6644 specifies and the harvest, pin and identity check are unchanged.
